title: Solace Harbor implementation standup and access handoff
next_steps: Redwood to share staging access checklist and runbook by 2026-09-21
Customer to provision VPC peering/NGW and share connectivity test results by 2026-09-24
Schedule pilot performance window (100k tokens/day) week of 2026-09-28
action_items: Maya Chen: Send staging access checklist + sample curl commands (due 2026-09-21)
Mark Reynolds: Provide VPC subnet CIDRs and k8s ingress IPs (due 2026-09-24)
Roberto Diaz: Prepare baseline workload test script and perf dashboard link (due 2026-09-23)
Ethan Brooks: Confirm required audit log retention and KMS key policy (due 2026-09-25)
summary: Kickoff standup to align implementation runbook, exchange staging access, and confirm security/observability requirements. Primary focus: VPC connectivity, API key provisioning, baseline perf tests, and timeline for pilot ramp. Several questions on dedicated vs hosted models, data residency and audit logs were discussed.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone, thanks for hopping on. well do a quick intro then go through the onboarding checklist. avatar, ava? actually Ava, wanna kick off?
[00:06] Ava Patel: Sure uh thanks Maya. Hi all, I'm Ava, CTO at Solace Harbor. We're trying to get Redwood into a pilot for our customer support summarization pipeline. timeline is roughly end of Sept to start smoke tests.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Cool. Roberto and I will run through staging access and then the SE bits on perf. Roberto, you wanna jump in?
[00:20] Roberto Diaz: Yep, thanks. hi team. quick note — we have two common deployment patterns: hosted API (fastest) and private VPC deployment. Based on notes earlier you wanted data to remain in your VPC and use your KMS?
[00:31] Mark Reynolds: Correct. we need customer-managed keys and audit logging. we are also leaning on a private deployment because of PII policy.
[00:37] Roberto Diaz: Got it. Private deployment supports customer KMS integration and audit logs. small caveat on dedicated vs private: dedicated is Redwood-managed infra reserved to you, private gives you a private control plane + optional on-prem. we'll map the exact network steps in the checklist.
[00:50] [00:51] Simone Li: Quick Q — what's the difference for latency? our SLA target is sub-150ms tail for 32-token replies in the summarization flow.
[00:58] Roberto Diaz: Good question. hosted typically has lower median latency because of multi-tenant autoscaling; private can hit similar latencies but depends on instance types and whether you use batching. For tail latency, we recommend smaller batch windows and dedicated GPU pools for predictable tails.
[01:11] Ava Patel: And cost tradeoff?
[01:12] Roberto Diaz: Dedicated equals higher committed cost but predictable unit cost. private self-managed adds infra ops overhead. We'll provide sample cost per 1M tokens for both profiles in the runbook.
[01:23] [01:25] Ethan Brooks: from security: we need SOC2 alignment, also SAML SSO for Redwood Console, RBAC per role, and long-term audit log retention (7 years ideally). can you support that?
[01:36] Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC2 and SAML SSO support, RBAC in console; audit export can be forwarded to your cloud storage. 7 years is longer than typical but we can model a retention export schedule — we'll include export patterns in the security doc.
[01:48] Ethan Brooks: also KMS: do you require cross-account roles or can we attach our key policies?
[01:52] Roberto Diaz: For private, you provide the KMS key and our control plane will request access via assumed role. We can provide an IAM policy template to keep things precise.
[02:03] [02:05] Mark Reynolds: network wise we have a couple of constraints: our egress is NAT'd through a single NGW and we use strict egress allowlists. how do we test connectivity?
[02:13] Roberto Diaz: We have a connectivity test script — curl to a staging endpoint and a small TLS handshake test. We'll push the script to the runbook. for VPC peering we can accept either VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your infra org preference.
[02:25] Maya Chen: action: well send the staging checklist with the test script and sample curl auth headers. Mark you'll paste the CIDR and the NAT gateway egress IPs.
[02:34] [02:36] Ava Patel: Great. on API credentials — do you support temporary tokens/STS or only long lived keys?
[02:42] Roberto Diaz: Both. For pilot we usually provision a scoped API key for the staging environment; for production private deployments we prefer temporary STS tokens with rotating roles.
[02:53] Simone Li: about observability — we want request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdown per route. can we map logs back to our internal ticket ids automatically?
[03:02] Roberto Diaz: Yes, we support custom metadata fields on requests that persist through logs and tracing. you can tag with ticket id and user id. the console will show token cost per request and we can surface custom tags.
[03:15] [03:17] Ethan Brooks: one more security item — will you allow egress filtering to prevent model updates outside our release window?
[03:22] Roberto Diaz: We provide model pinning and rollout controls. you can pin a model version and we have a canary rollout policy. automatic external updates won't happen without your rollout config.
[03:33] Maya Chen: okay moving to perf baseline — Roberto do you want to outline the 72-hour perf window?
[03:38] Roberto Diaz: Sure. recommended: 72-hour baseline with steady ramp to 100k tokens/day, with spike tests at 2x and 4x. We'll run sampling workloads: typical short summarization calls, also a smaller fraction of large transcripts to exercise KV cache. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, GPU utilization, and per-request token cost.
[03:59] Ava Patel: if p99 > 500ms we will need fallback options. what's the fallback?
[04:03] Roberto Diaz: fallback options: 1) smaller model variant pinned for latency-sensitive routes, 2) enable prefix caching for repeated support threads, 3) route to a hosted low-latency endpoint as warm fallback. we can configure automatic fallback policies.
[04:18] [04:20] Mark Reynolds: How intrusive is prefix/KV caching? does it store any PII on Redwood side?
[04:26] Roberto Diaz: Cache control is configurable. For private deployments, cache can be stored within your VPC; for hosted, we recommend encrypting and TTL controls. We'll include the cache policy options in runbook; default is not to persist PII.
[04:40] Simone Li: onboarding timeline — what are the immediate next few checkpoints?
[04:44] Maya Chen: We propose: (1) staging access checklist shared within 24-48 hours, (2) customer completes network prep & shares CIDRs in 4 business days, (3) Redwood provisions staging credentials and a sample dataset ingest, (4) start 72-hour perf window once network/creds validated.
[04:58] [05:00] Ava Patel: that sounds good. question — do you provide sample evaluation harness or should we reuse our in-house pytest harness?
[05:07] Roberto Diaz: We have a lightweight harness in Python and k6 scripts. We'll share both; you can plug in your ticket-id tags. If you already have a harness, we can adapt it.
[05:16] Ethan Brooks: compliance question: we need evidence for encryption-in-transit and at-rest — do you provide certs and architecture diagrams?
[05:23] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share SOC2 attestation, architecture diagram for private deployment, and KMS policy templates.
[05:30] [05:31] Mark Reynolds: small ops note — does Redwood support automated Terraform modules for the VPC peering and role setup?
[05:36] Roberto Diaz: We provide Terraform snippets and CloudFormation templates for AWS — we'll add them to the runbook repo.
[05:42] Simone Li: product question — can we call function-calling style structured outputs for the summarizer so downstream systems can parse easily?
[05:50] Roberto Diaz: Yes, we support structured output and function-style tool calls. We'll share examples of JSON schema enforcement and verifier hooks.
[05:58] [06:00] Ava Patel: ok can we talk SLAs — if we commit to pilot and scale, what SLA tiers are available?
[06:05] Maya Chen: Hosted has standard uptime SLA, Dedicated has tighter SLOs, and Private can be part of an enterprise contract with custom SLA. we'll route you to the commercial team for exact SLA numbers but we can give you typical latency SLOs per tier in the runbook.
[06:19] Mark Reynolds: any immediate blockers?
[06:21] Maya Chen: Not on our side — main blocker is network config and KMS policy from Solace Harbor. Once we have CIDRs + NGW IPs and KMS policy we can provision staging.
[06:31] [06:33] Simone Li: thanks. small ask: after you send docs, can we have a short 30-min runbook walkthrough next week?
[06:38] Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll send an invite for a runbook walk-through — propose 2026-09-22 or 23.
[06:44] Ava Patel: 23rd works for us.
[06:46] Maya Chen: Perfect. final recap — we'll: send staging checklist + connectivity script + Terraform snippets + security pack (SOC2 + KMS template) by 2026-09-21. Solace Harbor to share CIDRs, NGW IPs, and any additional compliance constraints by 2026-09-24. Redwood to provision staging creds and start scheduling perf window once validated.
[06:59] [07:00] Ethan Brooks: one last: can you add a note about long-term log export patterns in the runbook?
[07:04] Roberto Diaz: noted — will include export pattern examples to S3 and retention lifecycle rules.
[07:09] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. see you on the 23rd for the runbook walkthrough.
[07:15] Ava Patel: thanks all. bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "NGW" transcribed sometimes as "engy" in auto captions; some product names may be truncated.
